The Gwalior State page has Ajmer ceded again in 1818. The page lists Isagarh, Bhilsa, Narwar and Sheopur among the seven zilas of the 1947 state but dates none of them; they are drawn from 1818, when the treaty "readjusted boundaries". The counterpart is a guess at the Peshwa's and Malwa's lesser chiefs. Repair 2026-10-25: Bhopal State is cut out of the Isagarh and Bhilsa circles. Pages tried for a date and silent: Treaty of Gwalior (the Asirgarh fort only), Narwar (no transfer to the Scindias), Sheopur (the Gaurs ruled until they "succumbed to the Scindias", undated); confidence stays 1.

region.text: the Gwalior country between the Chambal and the capital

ledger.note: December 1843: Gough's army crosses the Chambal. "A British force under Sir Hugh Gough moved on Gwalior, and crossed the Chambal in December 1843."

region.text: the Gwalior country between the Chambal and the capital

ledger.note: 29 December 1843: Maharajpur and Punniar are fought and the Gwalior army is beaten. "the battles of Maharajpore and Punniar both fought on 29 December 1843"; "After the defeat of the Scindia forces in Gwalior, the British disbanded their army and established a force in the state."

region.text: Chanderi

ledger.note: 1844: Chanderi District is ceded to maintain the British contingent. "Under the subsequent treaty, lands including Chanderi District were ceded to fund a contingent force." The page does not date the treaty; the year follows the December 1843 campaign. Pages tried for the date: the Gwalior campaign page has no treaty; the Jayajirao Scindia page has the lands "including Chanderi District" ceded for a contingent force (worth 1.8 million, other lands for the war expenses) and no date, so the year stays a bridge from December 1843.

region.text: Chanderi District west of the Betwa River and the Chanderi State

ledger.note: 1858: Jayajirao is rewarded for loyalty in the Rebellion. Rose captured Gwalior on 17 June 1858 and reinstated him; "including the portion of Chanderi District west of the Betwa River, were granted to him" and "Gwalior annexed Chanderi State in the same year".

region.text: Jhansi city and a dependent territory

ledger.note: 1861: Jhansi city and a dependent territory are ceded to Gwalior. "In 1861, the city and a dependent territory were ceded to Gwalior State" (the Jhansi State page; the Siege of Jhansi page is silent on it). The extent of the dependent territory is not given; the city circle stands for it.

region.text: Gwalior fort and Morar cantonment

ledger.note: 1885: the British return Gwalior fort and Morar cantonment in an exchange for Jhansi city. "Gwalior fort and Morar cantonment, with some other villages, ... were exchanged for Jhansi city." The Jhansi State page dates the return to 1886: the city "was returned to British rule in exchange for the Gwalior Fort and the cantonment of Morar nearby". The Jayajirao Scindia page also puts the exchange in 1886.

region.text: Jhansi city

ledger.note: 1885: Scindia gives up Jhansi city in the exchange for the Gwalior fort and Morar cantonment.

region.text: the 1947 state, 64,856 km2

ledger.note: 1948: Gwalior joins Madhya Bharat. Infobox: accession to the Dominion of India 15 June 1948; Jivajirao became the first Rajpramukh of Madhya Bharat on 28 May 1948 and its instrument of accession took effect on 13 September 1948; merged into Madhya Pradesh 31 October 1956.

wars.name: Rajput campaigns of Mahadji Shinde
belligerents: Rajput kingdoms of Jaipur and Jodhpur

zones.text: the Rajput country about Lalsot, Patan and Merta

wars.outcome: Mahadji was repulsed at Lalsot (1787) and then crushed Jodhpur and Jaipur at Patan (20 June 1790) and Merta (10 September 1790). After Merta the Rathor ruler of Jodhpur gave the Scindias the province of Ajmer (Battle of Merta page, undated).

wars.name: Second Anglo-Maratha War

minus.text: the Nawab of Awadh's land (Cliopatria 1796 shape, as nawab-of-awadh draws 1794-1800)

union.text: the upper Ganges-Jamuna Doab (Aligarh, Meerut, Saharanpur side): the gazetteer's Doab less the lower Doab and Rohilkhand that the Nawab of Awadh held (Kora, Fatehpur-Kanpur-Etawah side) and less the part that spills south of the Yamuna into Bundelkhand

minus.text: Bharatpur and Deeg, the independent Jat state (bharatpur-state)

zones.text: the northern conquests ceded 30 December 1803 (upper Doab, Delhi, Agra)

wars.outcome: British victory: Surji-Anjangaon (30 December 1803) took Scindia's northern lands; Gwalior and Gohad were taken and restored in 1805.
wars.note: Delhi, Assaye and Laswari fell in September and November 1803; the war runs 8 August 1803 to 24 December 1805 (infobox).

wars.name: Third Anglo-Maratha War
wars.outcome: Treaty of Gwalior (5 November 1817): Scindia agrees to help against the Pindaris and gives up Rajasthan; Ajmer is ceded in 1818.
wars.note: Infobox 5 November 1817 to 9 April 1819; Scindia was not at war with the British in the field.

wars.name: Gwalior campaign
wars.outcome: British victory at Maharajpur and Punniar on 29 December 1843; the Gwalior army was disbanded and a contingent established; Chanderi District ceded.

certainty.note: Chauth districts and conquests: the pages give towns and districts, not boundaries. The Chambal as northern limit from 1805 is a river line but the pages give no survey.
British treaties named districts from 1803 and the state had a recorded area (64,856 km2) in detached portions; the detached portions themselves are not drawn.

notes: Seven pages opened in the first pass (Gwalior State, Mahadji Shinde, Second and Third Anglo-Maratha War, Gwalior campaign, Gohad State, Jhansi State) and six in the repair of 2026-10-25 (Battle of Merta, Daulat Rao Scindia, Treaty of Gwalior, Jayajirao Scindia, Narwar, Sheopur; the repair also re-opened Second Anglo-Maratha War and Gwalior campaign). The Jhansi State page adds the 1861 cession of Jhansi city to Gwalior and dates its return to 1886 (the Gwalior State page: 1885). (1) A member of the Maratha confederacy until 1818: its land lies inside the maratha-empire Cliopatria shape, and Cliopatria's Maratha Empire 1820 and 1842 shapes that sa-05-d marked wrong belong to this state; the rendering agents must decide whether the confederacy members are drawn as sub-units or tinted. (2) The Gwalior State page and the Gohad page disagree on 1805: Gwalior says Gwalior and Gohad were restored to Scindia, Gohad says the British took Gohad and Dholpur went to Rana Kirat Singh; Dholpur's annexation by Gwalior is dated only to "between 1782 and December 1805" and is not drawn. (3) Dates of the northern prant (Isagarh, Bhilsa, Narwar, Sheopur), Ajmer, the Doab/Haryana block and the 1844 cession are bridged at confidence 1 where the pages are silent. (4) British paramountcy: british-empire (sa-06) should record a vassal_start for gwalior-state from 5 November 1817 (Treaty of Gwalior; infobox "Protectorate of the East India Company 1818-1857"), british-raj from 1859 to 1947, republic-of-india for 1947-48. (5) Counterparts needing dossiers: gohad-state, madhya-bharat. (6) Gazetteer lacks Sheopur, Isagarh, Bhilsa, Narwar, Shajapur, Mandsaur, Amjhera, Chanderi, Broach, Hisar as places; circles by coordinates are used. (7) Wikipedia's Gwalior page: area 68,291 km2 (infobox) vs 64,856 km2 (body); the repaired shape measures about 59,179 km2. REPAIR 2026-10-25 (review sa-05-x, verdict fail). (a) The Doab was the gazetteer's whole region (135,554 km2, east to Allahabad) and so lay on the Nawab of Awadh's land (nawab-of-awadh: Kora, Allahabad and the Fatehpur-Kanpur-Etawah side from 1775, ceded to the British in 1801); it is now the Doab less Cliopatria's Awadh 1796 shape (what nawab-of-awadh draws 1794-1800, 253 of the Doab's 536 cells) and cut at about 26.6 N, which also removes 86 cells of the gazetteer region that spill south of the Yamuna into Bundelkhand (Jhansi, Banda, Hamirpur). The reviewer suggested the Cliopatria 1790 shape; I used the 1796 shape because the Awadh dossier's 1788-1800 keyframes all contain it (the 1790 shape leaves 79 cells of Rohilkhand-side Doab that nawab-of-awadh holds). KF 1788 falls from about 183,600 km2 to 83,457 km2, KF 1790 from about 194,500 to 93,067 km2. (b) Overlaps with sibling dossiers cut out: Bharatpur 60 km from the Agra and Mathura side (29 cells), Indore State's districts from the Malwa circles (29 cells from 1767; 14 cells against Indore's 1732-1766 circle, so the first keyframe is split at 1767), Bhopal State's polygon from the Isagarh and Bhilsa circles (17 cells), the Jaipur 90 km circle from the Ajmer circle (5 cells) and the Jhansi 36 km circle from the Bundelkhand circle of the 1803 loss. One cell is still shared with Indore: Ujjain city, the capital until 1810, lies inside Indore's 52 km circle and is kept in Gwalior (indore-state, a thin dossier not touched here, should trim its Indore circle). The Malwa part is now about 14,200 km2 against 20,774 km2 on the page and the 1947 total about 59,179 km2 against 68,291 km2 (infobox): the circles cannot both keep the page figures. (c) Thin items tried: Ajmer is now dated to 1790 at confidence 2 from the Battle of Merta page (counterpart kingdom-of-marwar, whose dossier lacks the matching loss); the dates of the Delhi-Agra and Doab block, of Isagarh, Bhilsa, Narwar and Sheopur and of the Chanderi treaty stay confidence 1 because Daulat Rao Scindia, Treaty of Gwalior, Gwalior campaign, Jayajirao Scindia, Narwar and Sheopur are silent on them. The Jayajirao Scindia page dates the Jhansi-for-Gwalior exchange to 1886, as the Jhansi State page does; only the Gwalior State page says 1885.
